title: The rich region around the Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The Tarantula Nebula and its surroundings in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Star clusters, glowing clouds of gas and the scattered remains of supernova explosions spread across this detailed view from the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. The main attraction is the Tarantula Nebula, glowing brightly in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
About 160 000 light-years away, the Tarantula is the Large Magellanic Cloud's most spectacular feature. The VST captured both the nebula and its rich surroundings in great detail.

A nebula like this is a vast cloud of gas and dust where new stars form, and hot young stars make the gas glow. Supernova remnants are the expanding debris of massive stars that have exploded, so the region holds both newborn stars and the debris of dead ones.
scale: The Tarantula Nebula lies about 160 000 light-years away, according to ESO.

understand.summary: This image from OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope combines g, r, i and hydrogen-alpha filters, covering visible light and the edge of the near-infrared. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.

explore: The image was built with OmegaCAM, the survey telescope's camera, from exposures through several filters, including one that isolates the red glow of hydrogen. The field lies in the direction of the constellation Dorado.
alt: A wide landscape of star clusters, glowing gas clouds and supernova remains around the Tarantula Nebula.
